issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the provided solution implement and call singFarmSong(). This naming inconsistency (method name/signature mismatch) can confuse students about which method they are expected to implement and may lead to compilation problems if students follow the problem text literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to request singFarmSong() (and mention singFarmSong in the instructions), or change the template and solution to provide/use printFarmSong() (with singFarmSong kept or forwarded to it). Ensure the method name used in examples (Main.java) and in the description match the method declared in the template.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement printFarmSong() as the method that prints the Old MacDonald song, but both the template and the solution use the method name singFarmSong() for the exact same functionality. This mismatch between the documented API (problem) and the provided code (template/solution) can confuse students who will look for printFarmSong() in the starter code and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either (a) update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() instead of printFarmSong(), or (b) rename the method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() so the documented API and code match.
